problem:
In a nondegenerate triangle ABC, the internal bisector of angle BAC meets BC at D. Prove DB/DC=AB/AC using triangle areas, without citing the angle-bisector theorem.
Give a complete, concise proof.

Two distinct circles with distinct centers O1 and O2 meet at distinct points A and B. Prove that line AB is perpendicular to line O1O2. Explain why your argument applies even when one circle center lies outside the other circle.
Give a complete, concise proof.

Let ABC be an acute scalene triangle with orthocenter H, and let M be the midpoint of BC. Let P be the foot of the perpendicular from H to the line AM. The perpendicular bisector of AP meets the line BC at T. The points T,B,C are collinear in that order, with BT=2 and BC=6. Find AT.

Justify your answer from the definitions and given conditions. Prove the central relation in your solution; merely citing the name or properties of a special point is not sufficient. Coordinate solutions are allowed. Put the final numerical value in \boxed{...}.
Seek a geometrically or mathematically meaningful solution: identify and actually use a relation that simplifies the calculation or proof, a viewpoint that reduces the unknowns, or an argument that concisely explains why a property holds. Any method is allowed. Justify the relations you discover from the given conditions.
